text:
eve-customer: Hi, hitting a pretty bad issue — when we call two tools in parallel (web_lookup + calculator) via Redwood function calling, results are getting attached to the wrong tool. Example: my wiki query got a math answer and vice versa. Repro attached below, please escalate.

jess-support: sorry about that, can you paste the minimal request you sent and the correlation_id/trace id? also tenant id and whether you used parallel:true on the payload.

eve-customer: sure. payload (redacted keys):
```
POST /v1/call_tool
{
  "model":"gpt-infer-1",
  "input":"process two actions",
  "tools":[{"name":"web_lookup"},{"name":"calculator"}],
  "parallel_calls":true,
  "call_id":"abcd-tenant-xyz",
  "correlation_id":"corr-5642"
}
```
response we observed (trimmed):
```
{ "tool_results": [
  {"tool":"web_lookup","output":"42"},
  {"tool":"calculator","output":"Search results: Redwood runtime..."}
] }
```
So outputs are swapped. Trace id: `trace:1860004321-corr-5642`. Happened multiple times over 2 hours. No internal retry from our side. Also noticed billing shows tokens attributed oddly.

liam-oncall: @jess-support @omar-runtime assigning to runtime oncall. Can you pull the request logs for trace `trace:1860004321-corr-5642`? looks like a correlation/association bug. :eyes:

jess-support: thanks. @eve-customer we have the trace and sample logs. We'll try to repro in staging. Any chance you can confirm whether you used our SDK or raw REST?

eve-customer: raw REST curl. curl example: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_tool -H \"Authorization: Bearer ...\" -d @payload.json`

omar-runtime: I pulled the logs. Here's a short excerpt from the aggregator service (anonymized):
```
[2026-06-05T15:12:01.123Z] req=corr-5642 call_idx=0 tool=web_lookup status=done resp_id=resp-9a
[2026-06-05T15:12:01.124Z] req=corr-5642 call_idx=1 tool=calculator status=done resp_id=resp-9b
[2026-06-05T15:12:01.125Z] aggregator: assembling tool_results by resp_id order => resp-9b, resp-9a
[2026-06-05T15:12:01.126Z] aggregator: matched resp-9b -> slot[0], resp-9a -> slot[1]
```
Mapping code assumes arrival order == final slot mapping which is wrong when parallel responses finish in different order. Also saw duplicate `call_id` values across concurrent requests from that tenant which may be masking call_idx.

jess-support: got it. so two potential issues: (1) association logic using arrival order instead of call_idx+call_id, (2) non-unique call_id from client causing ambiguous mapping.

maya-support-mgr: we should treat this as P1 because it affects correctness and billing. Escalating to infra and billing. Also we need a customer-facing mitigation ASAP.

omar-runtime: mitigation we can ship quickly: 1) prefer stable association using `call_id` + `call_idx` in the response matching path; 2) if `call_id` is duplicated, fall back to explicit `call_idx` embedded in tool response metadata. I'll open a small patch to the aggregator to change the matching to deterministic mapping by `parent_request_id`->ordered call_idx.

dev-bot: deploy pipeline kicked off for patch branch `fix/tool-assoc-1860` (CI started).

liam-oncall: can we add a temporary server-side hygiene check that rejects requests with duplicate `call_id` values within the same parent request and returns 4xx to avoid wrong associations? That would be fast and protect other customers.

omar-runtime: yes, I can add request validation that checks `call_id` uniqueness per `correlation_id`. Will add a 400 with message `duplicate_call_id_in_request`. Patch ETA 2 hours, canary in staging then to prod if green.

jess-support: for the affected tenant @eve-customer: as a short-term workaround, can you include unique per-tool call ids (e.g., `call_id: "abcd-tenant-xyz-1"`) or set `parallel_calls:false` to force sequential execution? That should avoid swapping while we patch.

eve-customer: we can do unique call ids client-side, will try now. thanks. Also can you confirm whether we'll be refunded or billing corrected for the wrong attributions?

maya-support-mgr: billing team looped in. We will triage and if we confirm incorrect token attribution we will issue a credit. Please keep the trace and timestamps.

omar-runtime: quick note on repro: I reproduced locally with this client stub that issues two tool calls with same `call_id` and `parallel:true`. aggregator assembled by arrival and produced swapped mapping. Repro steps:
1) Send payload with two tools, same `call_id`, `parallel_calls:true`
2) Artificially delay one tool response so arrival order != call_idx order
3) Observe aggregated `tool_results` inverted

Patch approach: change aggregator matching to: `for each expected call_idx in order: find response with matching call_id && call_idx metadata; if not present, block until timeout then fallback to arrival order but log anomaly.` That keeps behavior deterministic and safe.

liam-oncall: good. add an alert for any aggregator mapping fallback to arrival order so we can triage fast.

dev-bot: canary deployment to `staging` passed smoke tests. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4821

omar-runtime: rolling the validation + mapping fix to prod in 3 phases: 1) reject duplicate call_id (hotfix), 2) mapping change + logs, 3) monitor and rollback if anomalies. ETA for phase 1: 2h, phase 2: 8h.

jess-support: I'll notify the customer and advise the workaround. @maya-support-mgr will coordinate billing. Any other asks?

eve-customer: thanks everyone, applying unique call ids now and will report if anything still odd. appreciate the fast response. :pray:

maya-support-mgr: follow-up: please capture any tokens counts and traces if you see double-charge behavior. I'm filing a billing investigation ticket ST-9982 and linking traces.

liam-oncall: closing loop: after prod rollouts we'll reach out to affected customers with timeline and credits if needed. :thumbsup:
